verdict.rationale: First-party self-hosting docs say Supermemory runs on your own hardware as a single self-contained binary. They describe it as the same memory engine behind the hosted platform, with a local graph engine, local embeddings and a local LLM, and the pricing page lists a self-hosted option. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the self-hosted binary works as described, clarity on which plan or license tier grants self-hosting access and any feature parity limits.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Supermemory runs on your own hardware. It's the same memory engine behind the hosted platform... as a single self-contained binary.
Local graph engine, local embeddings, local LLM. Your data never leaves the building.
No Docker. No database to provision. No config files. It boots in seconds with everything built in
